content_html_sanitized:
Posted July 10, 2003
Analysis by Richard Cowan

The last week has seen a series of appalling ethical failures in dealing with cannabis, especially its medical use.

In the UK, MS patient Biz Ivol, was hounded for two years and then the prosecutors dropped the charges against her in the middle of her trial, thus depriving her of an opportunity to make her case before a jury.
See
All Power to The Incompetents: UK Cannabis Reform Delayed As Police Push for Arbitrary Power. Fail to Protect Royal Family, But Demand Control Over Cannabis. More That We Couldn't Make Up.

It was clear from the public reaction that a conviction was very unlikely. Ivol then attempted suicide, as she had said she would. She was rushed to a hospital and revived, but most of the UK media outside of Scotland ignored her plight, thus barring her from even making her case in the court of public opinion. See
Scottish MS Patient Says She Will Kill Herself When Trial Is Over. But GW Pharmaceutical's Research Proves That Her Death Will Really Be Murder. The Need for A Patients Rights Organization.

The Guardian, which has editorialized against prohibition, did not even mention her in a contemporaneous article on GW Pharmaceuticals, which nonetheless found space for a discussion of the hobbies of CEO Geoffrey Guy.
See
Dr. Lester Grinspoon Warns About The Pharmaceuticalization of Cannabis, As GW Pharmaceutical Hits All Time High After Deal With Bayer. But Does It Need Prohibition In Order to Succeed?

To make matters all the more squalid, the annual conference of the British Medical Association refused to call for allowing the use of cannabis for MS, even though the GW clinical trials of a whole cannabis extract have proven that cannabis is effective for MS. They also ignored Biz Ivol. Instead, they chose to focus on a new report that alleged that cannabis causes schizophrenia.
See
Classic Reefer Madness At London Times: " Woman who killed father 'driven mad by cannabis.' " Quacks and Hacks and Schizophrenia. Is It Paranoid to Distrust Politicized Science?

However, it was left to Health Canada to plumb the depths of intellectual and moral self-degradation. In keeping with that bureaucracy's practice of waiting until the last day legally allowed to pretend to obey a court order, yesterday they announced a phony medical cannabis program that is so transparently unworkable that it will probably be rejected by the courts, again.
From 2000 see
Health Canada Press Release Makes Clear that the Health of Canadians Is Less Important than Marijuana Prohibition. Victimization of a Patient Gives More Proof.

HC's announcement made very clear that this interim program was not being implemented to help patients, but to keep personal possession illegal in Ontario. Their press release even says, The interim policy announced today ensures that both the MMAR and prohibitions related to marihuana in Ontario will remain in effect. I would not count on it.
See
Government of Canada adopts interim policy on the provision of marihuana for medical purposes

An editorial in The Globe and Mail called it graceless. They might also have added mindless. This farce calls for Canadian doctors to distribute the HC cannabis from their offices for C$5 per gram (roughly US$3.50.)

A blend of weed from the Flin Flon mine will be sent by courier to the patient's doctor in 30-gram bags and will be limited to the amount that the doctor says is required to treat the patient's condition, which even an expert on cannabis would be hard pressed to do.

It is supposed to be standardized to a 10% THC content, but since HC knows nothing about cannabis there is no recognition of the role of the other cannabinoids.

The doctors are opposed to this for several reasons.

First, most of them are happy to use their ignorance as an excuse to do nothing.
See
Live Free or Die In Pain. The Ignorance and Arrogance of the Quacks Who Deny Pain Relief to the Sick and Dying.

However, in all fairness to them, HC has put them in an impossible position, again. B.C. Medical Association president Dr. John Turner said, " It boggles the mind. It sounds like a scheme thought up by a bureaucrat trying to make doctors' lives more difficult. "

" I mean, what would a doctor do with 10 totes of marijuana in the office cupboard? You would have to hope nobody breaks in to your office. I think most doctors would be absolutely horrified by this. "

To make matters worse, Health Minister Ann McLellan, AKA John Walters in drag, yesterday said, There have been no studies anywhere in the world that have been able to confirm medicinal benefit. "

She could take out an improvement patent on ignorance, but think about where that leaves Canadian doctors under Canada's socialized medicine. They are being asked to prescribe precise amounts of an illegal drug which the head of Health Canada says has no proven medical benefit. It is almost enough to make me feel sorry for quacks, but without the doctors cooperation the whole mess is a nonstarter.

Senator Pierre Claude Nolin, chair of the Canadian Senate committee that called for legalization said, " You can smell the bad faith of the government.''
See
Canadian Senator Stars At NORML Conference As DEAland Threatens Retaliation, Again. Rightwing Think Tank Cited As Semi-Official Source. Is Canada Still Too White To Invade? Bad Neighbor Policy?

Moreover, it only applies to the roughly 500 patients who have managed to get a federal exemption, so it does nothing for the thousands of others. Vancouver's BC Compassion Society alone has over 2,000 members and about that many more on a waiting list. Of course, HC could not begin to supply all of the patients in Canada.

The other part of the program calls for HC to sell 30 seeds for C$20 to patients who can grow, or get someone to grow for them. Of course, Steve Tuck, who gave HC the seed stock gives patients seeds, and many seed merchants offer them discounts, so this is no bargain, especially since there is no indication that anyone at HC knows anything about which seeds are which.

This is truly adding insult to injury as Canada is trying to send Tuck back to DEAland to be killed by the narcocracy after having taken his seeds. His original deal with them called for the cannabis to be given to the patients and to be used in research, but not sold. I hope he sues them.

More proof of the incompetence of Health Canada was demonstrated in the televised announcement by McLellan's spokesperson Cindy Cripps-Prawak, who went to great lengths to emphasize that HC hopes that the patients would eat or drink the cannabis, but not smoke it. There was no mention of vaporization even though I know that Hilary Black of Vancouver's Compassion Society and Philippe Lucas from Victoria's VICS, lectured them on the importance of vaporization at the recent meeting of the Medical marijuana stakeholders group.
See
No Medicine Is Smoked. Okay, But Why Isn't Cannabis Sold Over-the-Counter? New MAPS/NORML Vaporizer Study Undermines Key Part Of Prohibitionist Party Line On Smoked-Marijuana.
and
Health Canada's Office of Cannabis Medical Access' Stakeholder Advisory Committee Includes Physicians for A Smoke Free Canada - Not The Compassion Societies. But It Will Let Them Talk For An Hour

In short, this program is apt to be even more interim than HC had planned. It seems unlikely to satisfy the courts, because it certainly has not satisfied either the patients or the doctors. It is just one more example of victimizing the patients as a way of protecting prohibition.
See
What Is More Important, Prohibition Or The Patients? The Death of Cheryl Miller Should Remind Us All To Demand A Change In Priorities. Should Pain Be A Crime?

To end on a brighter note, I think that the refugee hearings for Ken Hayes went well. His hearings were briefer than those for Kubby and Tuck, in large part because many of the issues had been dealt with in those hearings.

California attorney Bill Panzer, a NORML Legal Committee member, testified about what would happen if Ken were forced to return to DEAland. He would be arrested at the border by the DEAland federal government and held without bail, and he would not be allowed even to mention medical use in his trial. Ironically, he would not even be eligible for the safety valve exemptions to the mandatory minimums in sentencing that allowed Ed Rosenthal to be sentenced to only one day in prison. (Plus 3 years supervision.) In a bit or fortuitous timing, word that the feds are appealing Rosenthal's one day sentence came just as Ken's hearings were ending.
See
Unequal Injustice: Rosenthal Sentenced to One Day, As Others Continue To Have Lives Ruined By Multi-Year Sentences. Analysis by Richard Cowan

It is clear that Ken could not get a fair trial by Canadian standards in DEAland federal courts. It remains to be seen whether that will keep Canada from sending him back, but I am optimistic.
See
Tuck Refugee Hearings End. The Facts Put Canada In Awkward Position. Catching A Nark In A Lie? Imagine That! News and Analysis by Richard Cowan.
